confirmed: Source: arXiv:2609.24859v1, 21 Sep 2026, full 19-page local PDF; the document title is Small-world Networks of Agents Brainstorm AI Risks, by Ke Zhou, Edyta Bogucka and Daniele Quercia (PDF p. 1). Appendix A.1-A.4, Tables 2-4 and Figures 5-7 are included (PDF pp. 14-19).
S1 is a model-configuration benchmark using a practitioner reference corpus, not a randomized human AI-assistance experiment or a synthesis (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 4-4.3; p. 15, Table 2).

S2 qualifies as a randomized people study: teams were randomly assigned to practitioner-generated or framework-generated risk reports, then produced Futures Wheel risk ideas whose counts were scored. The lab_rct workshop classification, ideas_supplied AI role, and with_ai fluency classification are consistent with the described study (PDF pp. 8-9, Sections 5-5.2; pp. 17-18, Figures 5-6).

The assigned sample comprises 40 people in 11 teams, with three to four people per team; five teams received practitioner reports and six received framework reports. People per arm are not reported and should remain null (PDF p. 2, Figure 1C; p. 9, Section 5.1).

Core exclusion and context_class none are correct: the entire recruited randomized sample has fewer than 50 people. The separate 45 practitioner contributors and five external expert raters cannot be added to that sample (PDF p. 6, Sections 4.1-4.2; p. 9, Section 5.1; codebook Section 3).

The reference corpus involved 45 AI practitioners in 8 workshops across 3 locations, lasting 1 hour and 45 minutes each, and contained 244 distinct risks. These are separate people and risk counts (PDF p. 6, Section 4.1; p. 16, Table 4).

The benchmark used 108 matched human risks and five external AI-domain expert raters. The matched-risk count is not a people count or a reported count of generated model outputs (PDF p. 6, Sections 4.2-4.3; p. 14, Appendix A.3).

S1-O1 reported values match: Small-world + Betweenness with Snowballing Typical Roles has Novelty 3.48, versus 2.32 for Single-turn LLM, normalized to a five-point Likert scale. The table and figure give no numerical uncertainty (PDF p. 15, Table 2; p. 7, Figure 2; p. 6, Section 4.2).

S2-O1 reported means match exactly: treatment versus control overall 21.1 versus 15.6; Level 1, 5.2 versus 5.2; Level 2, 8.7 versus 5.2; Level 3, 7.2 versus 5.2 (PDF p. 9, Section 5.2, first paragraph).

S2-O2 reported means match exactly: treatment versus control Human-Computer Interaction 8.2 versus 6.0; Socioeconomic & Environmental harms 5.6 versus 2.4; AI System Safety Failures & Limitations 3.5 versus 0.0. Privacy & Security is correctly recorded in control-versus-treatment order as 1.5 versus 1.0 (PDF p. 9, Section 5.2, second paragraph; Figure 4B).

The human-study outcomes are counts of risks per team, overall, by consequence layer, and within taxonomy categories; they are not counts of people, ratings, distinct categories, or similarity across different people. Neither an after_ai outcome nor a between-person diversity statistic is reported (PDF p. 9, Sections 5.1-5.2 and Figure 4).
The one-line finding correctly reports the 40-person, 11-team study and the means 21.1 versus 15.6, and correctly excludes it from core on sample size (PDF p. 9, Sections 5.1-5.2).

The implementation extends Plurals, but the underlying LLM name/version is not specified. The appendix contains no additional human-study arm-level people counts or definitions/numerical values for the Figure 4A error bars (PDF p. 14, Appendix A.1-A.3; pp. 15-19, tables and figures).

This is an empirical framework paper with two evaluations, not a review or meta-analysis; no pooled estimates, standardized synthesis effects or synthesis study count need to be filled (PDF pp. 5-10, Sections 4-6).
summary: The paper contains a team-randomized AI-assisted ideation study with 40 recruited people in 11 teams, so it remains below the 50-person core threshold. The reported means and source version match the PDF, but the analyzed-person count, undefined graphical error bars, reused-corpus provenance, company involvement, and incomplete comparison coding require correction.
